correctness.rationale: The recent square theorem supplies every nonlinear center-trivial constituent, while self-duality supplies the trivial constituent. Nontrivial linear twists of Steinberg are distinct irreducibles, so the square misses exactly those linears. If an irreducible chi were absent from the cube, chi St would be supported on at most d-1 missing linears, each with multiplicity at most one; this contradicts chi(1)St(1)>=q>d-1. The PGL_2(2) exception is checked directly.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Monteiro--Stasinski prove the nonlinear square-support input and replace Steinberg by another character for complete square support, but do not state the universal Steinberg-cube theorem or the exact 2/3 fixed-Steinberg covering exponent. The 2013 theorem concerns finite simple groups of Lie type, and classical/recent character-covering-number work studies a different group-wide invariant. Targeted searches found no matching PGL_n(q) Steinberg-cube result.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp all-n,q tensor-power classification for the Steinberg character of PGL_n(q), isolates the exact linear-character obstruction to the square, proves that one further factor always repairs it, and extends by twisting to full compatible central-character fibers in GL_n(q).

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
